text: The Patriots are navigating a significant secondary challenge heading into Week 2 against Pittsburgh, with starting cornerback Carlton Davis III downgraded to out after being listed as questionable, forcing New England to lean on depth in their defensive backfield against a Steelers team that will itself be missing starting wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. to a foot injury. On the brighter side, running back TreVeyon Henderson—who missed the opener with an ankle injury—declared himself "ready to go" for Sunday and is expected to return to the lineup, giving Drake Maye and the offense another weapon as they look to bounce back. In a separate matter, the organization honored Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro cornerback, who signed a one-day contract to retire as a member of the Patriots, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest corners in franchise history. The Patriots also elevated punter Mitch Wishnowsky from the practice squad for the second consecutive week, and owner Robert Kraft made headlines by explaining his decision to have Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming shows at Gillette Stadium, citing the artist's history of antisemitic rhetoric.
